subject.title: fix: keep the global loop breaker reachable after tool blocks

question: Which implementation should become the canonical fix for the global-breaker reachability bug: this PR’s explicit `ToolCallRecord.outcome` discriminant or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619’s sentinel result-hash approach?
rationale: Both branches target the same canonical bug, provide real behavior proof, and alter the central no-progress record contract differently; source evidence alone does not establish which representation maintainers want to preserve as the long-term invariant.

options.title: Adopt the typed outcome representation
options.body: Merge this PR after a current-head refresh, using `outcome: "loop-veto"` to keep detector-generated vetoes distinct from real hashes and other blocked outcomes.

options.title: Adopt the sentinel-hash representation
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619 if maintainers want to avoid extending the diagnostic record shape, then close this duplicate implementation.

options.title: Consolidate first
options.body: Ask one contributor to rebase a single canonical PR with the agreed representation and retain the strongest focused regressions from both branches.

recommendation.title: Adopt the typed outcome representation
recommendation.body: Merge this PR after a current-head refresh, using `outcome: "loop-veto"` to keep detector-generated vetoes distinct from real hashes and other blocked outcomes.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the clearest source-level diagnosis and distinction between this accounting defect and the separate termination behavior, though a current-main feature-history owner should make the final choice.
